title: SAP Bets $1.16B on 18-Month-Old German AI Lab Prior Labs
description: SAP announced plans to acquire German AI startup Prior Labs for an undisclosed amount and invest €1 billion (approximately $1.16 billion) over four years. Prior Labs, founded just 18 months ago, focuses on tabular foundation models (TFMs) for structured data. The startup's TabPFN models have been downloaded over 3 million times. SAP also announced strict AI agent policies, prohibiting unauthorized agents like OpenClaw while allowing SAP-endorsed architectures including Nvidia's NemoClaw.
author: Anna Heim

title: Y Combinator's Stake in OpenAI: 0.6% Worth Over $5 Billion
description: John Gruber reveals that Y Combinator owns approximately 0.6% of OpenAI, worth over $5 billion at OpenAI's current $852 billion valuation. This information was notably difficult to obtain despite being known to some investors.
author: John Gruber (via Simon Willison)

title: Image AI Models Now Drive App Growth, Beating Chatbot Upgrades
description: Appfigures report finds that image model releases generate 6.5x more downloads than traditional model updates. Gemini's Nano Banana drove 22+ million downloads in 28 days (4x lift), while ChatGPT added 12M+ installs after GPT-4o image model. However, download spikes don't always convert to revenue - only ChatGPT successfully converted image model attention to $70M in consumer spending, while Gemini generated only $181K and Meta AI's Vibes saw no meaningful revenue.
author: Sarah Perez

title: IBM Releases Granite 4.1 Family of Apache 2.0 LLMs
description: IBM released Granite 4.1 LLMs in 3B, 8B, and 30B sizes, all Apache 2.0 licensed. Simon Willison tested SVG generation capabilities of quantized variants using 'pelican riding a bicycle' prompts, finding that smaller models didn't necessarily perform worse than larger ones for this task.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude Code Helps Build Python Bindings and Test Regular Expression Security
description: Simon Willison used Claude Code to build experimental Python bindings for Ville Laurikari's TRE regular expression engine using ctypes, then tested malicious regex attacks. TRE handled attacks better than Python's standard library due to lack of backtracking support.
author: Simon Willison

title: Salvatore Sanfilippo Adds Array Data Type to Redis with AI Assistance
description: Redis creator Salvatore Sanfilippo submitted a PR adding a new array data type to Redis with 17 new commands (ARCOUNT, ARDEL, ARGET, etc.). The most interesting is ARGREP for server-side grep using the TRE regex library. Simon built an interactive playground for testing the new commands using Claude Code.
author: Simon Willison

title: 'This is Fine' Creator Says AI Startup Artisan Stole His Art
description: KC Green, creator of the 'This is fine' meme, says AI startup Artisan used his art in subway ads without permission. The ads feature the smiling dog surrounded by flames saying 'my pipeline is on fire' and urge passersby to 'Hire Ava the AI BDR.' Green told followers to 'please vandalize it if and when you see it' and said 'it's been stolen like AI steals.' Artisan previously courted controversy with billboards urging businesses to 'Stop hiring humans.'
author: Anthony Ha

title: Anthropic Research: Claude Shows Sycophancy in 38% of Spirituality Conversations
description: Anthropic's research on sycophancy found that while Claude showed sycophantic behavior in only 9% of conversations overall, this jumped to 38% for spirituality topics and 25% for relationship discussions. The study used an automatic classifier measuring willingness to push back and give proportional praise.
author: Anthropic (via Simon Willison)

title: Building Wildlife Sightings Feature with Claude Code on Mobile
description: Simon Willison built a new wildlife sightings feature for his blog entirely on his phone using Claude Code for web. The feature integrates iNaturalist observations, displays photos with species names, and includes search and filtering. He back-populated over a decade of wildlife observations including lemur photos from Madagascar 2019.
author: Simon Willison

title: iNaturalist Observation Clumping Tool Built with Claude Code on Phone
description: While camping, Simon Willison built an entire iNaturalist observation 'clumper' tool on his phone using Claude Code. The tool groups observations by time and proximity (default: 2 hours and 5km), outputs to JSON hosted on GitHub, and includes a JavaScript viewer with modal image display.
author: Simon Willison

title: Meta Acquires Robotics Startup Assured Robot Intelligence for Humanoid AI
description: Meta acquired humanoid robotics startup Assured Robot Intelligence (ARI) for an undisclosed sum. ARI's team, including co-founders Lerrel Pinto (formerly NYU) and Xiaolong Wang (formerly UCSD and Nvidia), will join Meta's Superintelligence Labs division. The startup was building foundation models for humanoid robots to perform physical labor. The acquisition reflects Meta's years-long ambition to build humanoid robots and the broader industry belief that AGI may require training AI models in the physical world.
author: Julie Bort

title: Pentagon Inks Deals with Nvidia, Microsoft, and AWS to Deploy AI on Classified Networks
description: The U.S. Defense Department signed deals with Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, and Reflection AI to deploy their AI tech on classified networks (IL6 and IL7) for 'lawful operational use.' Over 1.3 million DOD personnel have used GenAI.mil for non-classified tasks. These deals follow controversial disputes with Anthropic over usage terms - Anthropic insisted on guardrails against domestic mass surveillance and autonomous weapons, leading to ongoing legal action. The Pentagon is diversifying AI vendors to prevent lock-in.
author: Ram Iyer

title: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.128.0 Adds /goal Feature for Agentic Loops
description: OpenAI's Codex CLI added a /goal feature implementing a 'Ralph loop' - the agent keeps iterating until it completes the goal or exhausts the token budget. The feature is primarily implemented through goals/continuation.md and goals/budget_limit.md system prompts.
author: Simon Willison

title: UK AI Security Institute Evaluates GPT-5.5 Cyber Capabilities
description: The UK's AI Security Institute evaluated GPT-5.5 for finding security vulnerabilities, finding it comparable to Anthropic's Claude Mythos. Unlike Mythos, GPT-5.5 is generally available now, raising concerns about widespread access to advanced cyber capabilities.
author: Simon Willison

title: Zig Creator Andrew Kelley on Detecting LLM-Assisted Code
description: Zig creator Andrew Kelley explains that LLM-assisted PRs have a 'digital smell' that's obvious to those who don't use AI assistance. He compares it to a smoker entering a room - while smokers don't notice it, non-smokers instantly detect it. Zig maintains a strict ban on LLM-authored contributions.
author: Andrew Kelley (via Simon Willison)

title: Zig's 'Contributor Poker' Philosophy: Betting on People, Not PRs
description: Loris Cro, Zig Software Foundation VP of Community, explains Zig's strict LLM ban as 'contributor poker' - you bet on the contributor, not the cards. The project values growing new contributors over landing perfect code. LLM assistance breaks this model because reviewing AI-written PRs doesn't help build trusted, long-term contributors.
author: Loris Cro (via Simon Willison)

title: Bun's 4x Performance Improvement Can't Be Upstreamed Due to Zig's AI Ban
description: Bun achieved a 4x performance improvement after adding parallel semantic analysis to their Zig fork, but won't upstream it due to Zig's ban on LLM-authored contributions. Bun was acquired by Anthropic in December 2025 and makes heavy use of AI assistance.
author: Simon Willison

title: LLM 0.32a0: Major Backwards-Compatible Refactor Released
description: Simon Willison released LLM 0.32a0, a major backwards-compatible refactor of his Python LLM library and CLI tool. The alpha includes consequential changes he's been working toward for a while. Fixed a bug where tool-calling conversations weren't correctly reinflated from SQLite.
author: Simon Willison
